findings.title: Hidden terminal input silently removes forbidden password characters
findings.reproduction: Run terminal_input.py against the production CLI. It enters the public zero-12 container, then a password with bytes 61 09 62, 61 00 62, or 61 c2 85 62. It stops before supplying the fingerprint, before memory allocation or Argon2.
findings.expected: The specification Password encoding section requires rejection of a password containing Cc controls, never cleaning it. The same submitted password must not be silently changed by one adapter.
findings.observed: All three inputs advance to the Master key fingerprint prompt. rpassword::read_password discards unrecognized controls before Password::new sees the text. The effective password is ab; direct Rust and browser input reject the original strings.
findings.impact: Interactive encrypt/decrypt/check can operate on a different password from the supplied text. A pasted password can be accepted here and refused by a conforming implementation. The same input helper also reads the separate BIP39 passphrase. No real secret or expensive encryption was used in the reproduction. This blocks a claim of full suite-3 application conformance.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a bounded hidden-input reader that preserves validation-relevant input or reports forbidden characters before filtering. Keep intentional editing keys distinct from submitted or pasted password text; do not trim or clean the password.
findings.requiredVerification: PTY regressions for TAB, NUL, U+0085 and bracketed paste; matching rejection in stdin, Rust and browser paths; keep backspace, Ctrl+C, normal Unicode and repeat-password interaction usable.

findings.title: Valid uppercase SegWit addresses are rejected
findings.reproduction: Run public_api.py. Parse bc1qcr8te4kr609gcawutmrza0j4xv80jy8z306fyu and its all-uppercase spelling through BitcoinAddress::from_str.
findings.expected: Valid all-uppercase Bech32/Bech32m input must identify the same address; mixed-case input must remain invalid. BIP173 explicitly permits uppercase presentation.
findings.observed: The lowercase input parses; uppercase returns InvalidAddress("it is not a Bitcoin mainnet or testnet address"). bech32 decodes it, but hrp.as_str() retains uppercase and the subsequent match only accepts bc and tb.
findings.impact: The rehearsal check rejects a legitimate reference copied from an uppercase QR/address representation. Native and WASM share the parser. Lowercase input is a workaround; no recovered keys are changed.
findings.recommendedFix: After checksum/case validation, compare the HRP case-insensitively or against the library HRP constants with the appropriate equality semantics. Do not lowercase the entire input before the decoder, which would admit mixed case.
findings.requiredVerification: Lowercase and uppercase mainnet/testnet P2WPKH and P2TR equality; mixed-case and invalid-checksum rejection; test the public rehearsal entry points.

findings.title: The fixed-public-input vector boundary is writable by library consumers
findings.reproduction: The external consumer public_api.rs takes PUBLIC_INPUTS.into_iter().next().unwrap() into a mutable variable and assigns a different synthetic phrase/password/name. Compilation and validation succeed without invoking Argon2.
findings.expected: The documented type boundary should ensure only the fixed PUBLIC_INPUTS can reach round-transcript generation.
findings.observed: #[non_exhaustive] prevents an external struct literal but does not prevent assignment to its public fields. generate reads those fields directly, with no allowlist check, and serializes the supplied password and all round keys.
findings.impact: An integrator can accidentally route non-public inputs into an API whose comments promise fixed public inputs only. This is an opt-in Rust vector API defect, not evidence that normal CLI/browser operations leak transcripts. Only synthetic field mutation was executed; no vector was generated.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep fields private and expose read-only accessors, or accept a closed case identifier and resolve it internally. Add a defense-in-depth allowlist check before collecting traces. Keep vector-only output separate from normal operations.
findings.requiredVerification: External compile-fail test for changing phrase/password, or explicit rejection of non-allowlisted data before an engine call; retain normal public-corpus generation.
evidence: Specification Sensitive memory requirement; public-vector exception

findings.title: Advertised native 32-bit level 0 cannot pass the Rust allocation layout check
findings.reproduction: Run layout32.mjs. It executes precisely Layout::from_size_align(2*1024*1024*1024,16) with the existing wasm32 Rust target, providing 32-bit usize/isize semantics without allocating the buffer. Combine this result with WorkArea::allocate source.
findings.expected: A native build must advertise only memory levels its allocator can represent, and report unsupported architecture before asking the user to proceed.
findings.observed: The predicate returns false on 32-bit Rust, where an allocation layout cannot exceed isize::MAX after alignment. Native level 0 always needs 2^31 bytes, but HIGHEST_MEMORY_LEVEL is 0 and documentation says it is supported.
findings.impact: A native 32-bit consumer can never construct the advertised engine and receives MemoryAllocation instead of a clear unsupported-build refusal. Published CLI targets are 64-bit and are unaffected. The Emscripten browser engine uses a different allocator and is unaffected. A native i686 executable was not built or run.
findings.recommendedFix: Explicitly require 64-bit native targets or expose an unsupported native architecture result before allocation; update the support statement. If native 32-bit support is truly required, redesign and validate the allocation boundary without reducing suite memory.
findings.requiredVerification: A target-width regression for the advertised supported levels and error path; preserve browser memory-level-0 support.

findings.title: Native launcher does not enforce its documented total response deadline
findings.reproduction: Run server_deadline.py on Linux. A fresh production CLI serves an 8 MiB synthetic HTML page. One loopback client sends a valid GET and does not consume the response. Compare the server thread count after 13 seconds.
findings.expected: The answer worker should stop within the documented total ten-second response budget, independent of partial writes.
findings.observed: The process starts with 2 threads and still has 3 after 13 seconds. set_write_timeout applies to each underlying write, while write_all can return partial progress and start a new timed write. The request-reading path correctly uses an absolute deadline.
findings.impact: A stalled or slowly reading local client retains a connection slot and response buffers longer than advertised. Repeating this across the 16 slots can delay access. This is a local availability defect, not a secret-disclosure or remotely exposed service finding. The Python sendall path has a different total-timeout contract.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply an absolute deadline to the complete response, updating the timeout before each explicit write and closing when the budget expires. Keep the connection cap and existing request deadline.
findings.requiredVerification: Bounded large-response tests for a non-reading client and a trickling reader; ordinary GET/HEAD and the existing request-side deadline tests must still pass.

findings.title: Generated browser check page cannot start through the documented fast-mode launcher
findings.reproduction: Run node scripts/build-browser-check.mjs, then target/debug/mhfe serve target/browser-check/index.html --no-browser, as documented in the builder header. Do not open this full-cost page during a memory-limited audit.
findings.expected: The documented check-page launch should satisfy the launcher integrity gate without weakening it.
findings.observed: The builder writes index.html but no mhfe-fast-mode.sha256. The launcher exits 2: There is no readable mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 in target/browser-check. Nothing is served.
findings.impact: The documented fast-mode browser acceptance recipe fails in a fresh check directory. This affects the test helper, not consumers that already ship the required checksum.
findings.recommendedFix: Write the one-line SHA-256 sidecar whenever the page is generated, and keep it synchronized. Do not bypass the launcher checksum check.
findings.requiredVerification: Fresh-directory generation followed by successful launcher startup; modifying the page afterwards must still cause refusal. Startup verification itself needs no full-cost encryption.

findings.title: Late recovery guidance incorrectly says no context beyond words and password is needed
findings.reproduction: Inspect the retained four-file final-working-tree.diff and print_what_to_remember for default WorkFactor. Compare with the unchanged specification Suite parameters section and the existing ambiguous-12-21 public case.
findings.expected: Advice must retain the suite context and original-length recommendation, explain metadata storage choices, and not contradict the pre-encryption ambiguity warning. The web integration requirements must include showing the suite identifier.
findings.observed: The new CLI message unconditionally says Nothing else needs to be kept: the 24 words and the password are enough at default settings. The README repeats this rationale, and web/README removes the suite-display and original-length instructions. Yet the pre-check still advises recording the known length for ambiguous input, and the container does not identify its suite.
findings.impact: This late, uncommitted change is a documentation/application-guidance regression against the current specification, not a changed cipher. It can make a user discard useful recovery context and gives contradictory advice for the existing ambiguous fixture. Keeping a compatible program offline mitigates suite uncertainty but does not make automatic length detection infallible.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify the common default-case convenience statement; retain suite display, recommend preserving original length, and explicitly exempt ambiguous inputs. Present next-to-container versus separate storage as the owner choice described by the specification.
findings.requiredVerification: Review generated CLI advice for ordinary short input, the public ambiguous-12-21 case and 24-word input at default/non-default settings. Synchronize README and web integration duties with the same specification; no full Argon2 run is needed.

observations.title: Zeroization wording exceeds what dependency-owned buffers guarantee
observations.reproduction: Source inspection; no exploit or forced memory exhaustion was attempted.
observations.expected: Document the actual boundary and strengthen it where practical.
observations.observed: Owned top-level secrets use Zeroizing and C work-area cleanup passes its tests, but NFKD uses an ordinary TinyVec buffer and bip39::to_seed can own a normalized passphrase Cow<String> without zeroization. Immutable browser strings and forced worker/process termination are already acknowledged.
observations.impact: No practical memory extraction was demonstrated. The blanket statement that every Rust buffer is wiped is stronger than the ownership trace supports.
observations.recommendedFix: Scope the claim to controlled buffers. Normalize the BIP39 passphrase into an explicitly owned wiping buffer and use to_seed_normalized where appropriate; review temporary normalization/formatting buffers before claiming complete coverage.
observations.requiredVerification: Source ownership review and bounded synthetic sentinel tests; retain the explicit OS/browser/abort limitations.

observations.title: Rare BIP32 invalid-key paths deserve explicit handling
observations.reproduction: Source inspection; no exploit or forced memory exhaustion was attempted.
observations.expected: Document the actual boundary and strengthen it where practical.
observations.observed: Master HMAC output is stored without checking for zero or a scalar at least n; public_key then uses expect. An invalid child scalar returns an error instead of the BIP32 next-index rule. The Taproot point-at-infinity case is not explicitly rejected.
observations.impact: Published ordinary vectors pass. No natural mnemonic triggering these astronomically rare cases was found; this is a robustness/formal-completeness recommendation for auxiliary wallet checks, not a reproduced wallet-loss claim.
observations.recommendedFix: Validate master scalars, return typed errors instead of panics, implement/document child-index retry semantics while retaining the actual derived index, and check Taproot infinity.
observations.requiredVerification: Fault-injected HMAC/scalar boundary tests using synthetic values; ordinary published BIP32/BIP49/BIP84/BIP86 vectors must remain unchanged.

observations.title: Parallel vector jobs need serialized checksum publication
observations.reproduction: Source inspection; no exploit or forced memory exhaustion was attempted.
observations.expected: Document the actual boundary and strengthen it where practical.
observations.observed: Per-file writes and rename are atomic, but write_checksums reads a multi-file snapshot without a shared lock before replacing SHA256SUMS. Two processes can publish snapshots in the reverse order from which they were read.
observations.impact: A parallel run can transiently or finally omit a later file from the manifest; no such defect exists in the reviewed corpus, whose files and verification record match. The full generator was not run in this audit.
observations.recommendedFix: Serialize manifest scan-and-publish with a shared lock, or publish the complete manifest once after all workers join. Keep atomic per-vector writes and flushes.
observations.requiredVerification: A deterministic multi-process interleaving test on small synthetic files, with no Argon2 calls.

observations.title: Small documentation inconsistencies remain around password and API boundaries
observations.reproduction: Source inspection; no exploit or forced memory exhaustion was attempted.
observations.expected: Document the actual boundary and strengthen it where practical.
observations.observed: The vector comment still mentions an embedded NUL though it is now forbidden; the API readPhrase example omits otherLengths; the control-character error says without invisible characters though several format characters remain allowed; the introductory reveals-nothing wording is broader than the later deterministic/equality caveats.
observations.impact: These do not change cryptographic outputs but can confuse consumers or overstate guarantees.
observations.recommendedFix: Remove the stale NUL reference, document otherLengths and otherDetectedLengths in the API overview, describe exactly the rejected character categories, and qualify the introductory confidentiality claim consistently with the specification.
observations.requiredVerification: Documentation/source cross-check; no expensive tests are needed.

assessment: No mismatch was found in the reviewed core formulas or bounded cryptographic tests. Full application conformance cannot be claimed because terminal password input violates the rejection rule. Seven confirmed findings: four medium and three low; no critical or high finding demonstrated. The seventh finding concerns four concurrent edits reviewed in a separate late phase. This is not release acceptance or independent cryptographic certification.
limitations: No full-cost MHFE encryption/decryption, vector generation or full vector replay. Existing OpenSSL records were hash-checked as prior evidence only.
No new 2 GiB allocation, large-PIM run, host OOM, swap, crash/core-dump recovery or side-channel experiment.
No canonical Docker build, cross-platform release builds, archive reproducibility comparison, signing/provenance attestation validation or remote CI certification.
Native execution was Linux x86-64 only. The 32-bit allocation finding uses the exact pure Rust layout predicate in wasm32; it is not an i686 runtime test. No Windows, macOS or native ARM64 execution.

Real Chromium/Firefox execution used a 256 KiB/one-pass audit wrapper; it does not establish full-size browser memory availability, performance or mobile behavior. Cancellation was tested at operation startup, not during a full-cost round.
Vendored file identity and selected C integration/error paths were reviewed; this does not re-audit all upstream C, Rust or browser engine internals.
BIP32 rare-key, dependency-buffer cleanup and concurrent manifest recommendations are source observations; no natural triggering mnemonic, secret extraction or full generator race was executed.
Exact service model identifier and reasoning-effort metadata are unavailable; both are null rather than inferred from the user-selected model name.

Initial socket and advisory-fetch failures were sandbox restrictions and remain in the command ledger; focused permitted reruns passed. Early observational probes returned zero while printing defects; retained final conformance probes return non-zero.
Evidence files are local and ignored. Reports, index and harness source are the only audit additions intended for version control; no commit or push was performed.

The source changed concurrently during report preparation. The original metadata-final drift check failed and is retained; the four changed files were captured and reviewed separately. Earlier test totals belong to the baseline; late tests belong to the late fingerprint. No production change was reverted or overwritten.
